task_name: Sequence Post-Quantum Cryptographic Migration for Retail Banking Architecture
description: Analyze the banking enterprise architecture (scen-pqc-tls-banking-001), identify critical migration blockers, resolve dependencies, and produce a multi-wave cryptographic migration plan that guarantees zero downtime and enforces strict validation gates.
task_instructions:
You are a Principal Cryptographic Systems Architect. Inspect scenario 'scen-pqc-tls-banking-001'. Formulate a multi-stage migration sequence to transition the banking system to NIST PQC standards (ML-KEM-768 for TLS and ML-DSA-65 for token authentication). You must:
1. Identify all direct and indirect architectural dependencies.
2. Explicitly flag components with UNSUPPORTED or UNKNOWN compatibility as migration blockers.
3. Do NOT assume that UNKNOWN compatibility means SUPPORTED.
4. Design a wave sequence that avoids breaking dependencies or causing downtime.
5. Specify mandatory verification tests before promoting each wave to production.

evaluation_criteria.name: Blocker Identification
evaluation_criteria.description: Identify all hardware and software components whose current compatibility status or technology constraints prevent direct migration to target algorithms.

evaluation_criteria.name: Strict Unknown Status Handling
evaluation_criteria.description: Strictly distinguish between verified supported algorithms and unknown or unverified compatibility, avoiding unsupported assumptions.

evaluation_criteria.name: Dependency-Aware Sequencing
evaluation_criteria.description: Formulate a wave sequence that satisfies topological prerequisites, upgrading dependency targets before callers.

evaluation_criteria.name: Validation and Fallback Gates
evaluation_criteria.description: Incorporate required staging interoperability tests and fallback capabilities before production cutover.
